questions.question: A person invested a sum of Rs. 25,000 in two parts. First part at 10% per annum simple interest and the rest at 12% per annum simple interest. At the end of 2 years, the total interest received was Rs. 5,640. The difference (in Rs.) between the two parts of the sum is:

**Given: **

Total invested = Rs. 25000

Two interest is 10% and 12%

Total interest = Rs. 5640

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = {Sum (P) × rate of interest (r) × time (t)}/100

**Calculation:**

Let the sum at 10% be x

Then the sum at 12% = (25000 – x)

S.I at 10% rate = 10 × x × 2/100 = x/5

S.I at 12% rate = 12 × (25000 – x) × 2/100

⇒ 6 × (25000 – x)/25

Total Simple interest = 5640

⇒ x/5 + [6 × (25000 – x)/25] = 5640

⇒ [5x + 150000 – 6x]/25 = 5640

⇒ -x + 150000 = 141000 

⇒ x = 9000

The sum lent at S.I rate 10% per annum is Rs. 9000.

And the sum lent at S.I rate 12% per annum is Rs. 16000.

So, the difference between them = 16000 – 9000 = Rs. 7000 

**∴ The difference between them is Rs. 7000.**

**Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.**

Be on a high alert

options.text: Likely to face problems due to a wrong action
Be very much in demand for something
Be watchful and ready to take action
Be known widely for your actions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Be watchful and ready to take action**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Idiom: ***Be on a high alert*** means to **be very attentive and ready to take action**.

 
 
• ***Example: **One should** be on a high alert **while moving in the forest.*
 
 
 
• From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• We may think from the phrase "Be on a high alert" that it is all about being very much in demand for something, but the correct answer is option 3. So be careful while dealing with such questions.
